scope: Extend whole-operation ASCII and Binary DXF allocation-failure coverage from the rich BLOCK_RECORD route to every public writeBlockRecord overload, preserving fields relevant to each overload and checking typed readback.

source.profile: A generated AC1032 drawing with one named BLOCK_RECORD and two INSERTs. Four writer routes are exercised: (1) name and insertion units, (2) name, units, and preview bytes, (3) name, units, preview bytes, and ordered INSERT source handles, and (4) the same plus APPID/XDATA. Fields omitted by a route are verified absent; supplied references are checked against emitted INSERT identities.

implementation.change: Parameterized the focused BLOCK_RECORD whole-operation allocation sweep to invoke all four public overloads. Readback checks name, insertion units, optional preview data, optional ordered/remapped INSERT handles, and optional APPID/XDATA. Existing source model, caller preservation, identity rollback, stage cleanup, and retry checks apply to every variant.
implementation.method: For each overload and each ASCII/Binary encoding, calibrate allocation count from a successful clean export, inject std::bad_alloc at every reached offset with a prior destination sentinel, require failure and exact destination/source preservation plus identity-ledger rollback and stage cleanup, then retry the same codec and require byte-identical output and fresh typed readback.

validation.result: All 8 overload/encoding combinations passed rollback, same-codec retry, byte-identical output, caller preservation, stage cleanup, and typed readback.

limitations: Generated output transaction and typed readback evidence only; no producer-authored preview semantics, broad BLOCK_RECORD graph closure, or native consumer claim follows.
The profile uses AC1032. Legacy version-specific admission and producer interoperability remain separate qualification work.
No DWG/DXF fixture files were added, and no support claim is promoted.

planImpact.completedSlice: Transaction and typed readback coverage for all four public BLOCK_RECORD writer overloads, extending the prior rich-overload-only profile.
